account:
Today I have kept my office, mill inspection, lunch, and council letters appointments, and am now at my neighbour's east-bank cottage for fifteen o'clock tea. There were no council letters for me to review. My next ordinary appointment is the office at sixteen-thirty.

The unusual business is a large gathering being prepared in the town hall. Lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw both the builder and innkeeper deposit bread in a hall table chest. The baker told me that the innkeeper had confirmed delivery of two hundred feast loaves. The builder appears to be coordinating supplies and lighting. Today the builder explicitly invited me to the hall at eighteen, said the innkeeper would escort me, and asked that I indulge them in keeping the occasion's details until then. The secretary reports that the innkeeper called it community hospitality, with the programme announced at eighteen and no prepared remarks needed from me.

My best guess is a deliberately concealed surprise celebration or community feast, perhaps intended in my honour, though nobody has confirmed its purpose. The secrecy now seems intentional rather than merely poor communication. I have no evidence that it is something hostile or improper.

There are also repeated rumours about a bridge or port change at the bakery. I heard townsfolk repeat them, but the baker explicitly said there was no verified bridge or ferry change. My neighbour agreed not to pass on those rumours. I cannot connect them to the hall preparations on the evidence I have. I have asked my neighbour for other town news and am awaiting an answer.
